observations: All four native facings show a clear rounded-square blue upholstered seat over warm honey-brown legs and a structural crossbar. Cushion corners and sidewalls now have continuous soft rounding, and the prior sharp cyan panel and stacked royal-blue bevel strips are replaced with a coherent softly shaded blue volume.

The honey wood is materially brighter and warmer than the original nearly black legs. Feet, lower faces and crossbar remain visible on light, neutral and dark backgrounds; natural joints and the open gap below the seat read cleanly. The slight crossbar-height difference between N/S and E/W is consistent with the preserved native stool construction.

Lighting remains horizontally balanced across the four rotations. Broad edge transitions and gentle local shading describe form without blown white spots, hard highlight bands or a directional cast ground shadow.

At logical size, all facings retain a clean padded-seat silhouette and leg/support separation. Native views and enlargement show no material black patches, clipped corners, opaque filling of openings, coplanar interference, harsh normal seams or colored target halo. The repeated preview is coherent at one-cell pitch.

Material variation is restrained. The candidate is simpler and more matte than the imagegen target, but the cushion reads as soft upholstery and the warm supports retain their wood identity without competing texture or noise. This satisfies the frozen criterion that large-form readability takes precedence over target microtexture.
